Risto Pakkanen DISCOVERY CONFIRMED
SpaHotel Hamina (old hotel)
Breakfast at the SpaHotel
Getting thereSibeliuskatu 32, 49400 Hamina, Finland  ·  open in Maps
From Hotelli Jokipuisto — crew11.3 mi · 17 minFrom SpaHotel Hamina0.0 mi · 0 min
For Nick & the crewA Hamina lifer in his 60s who has survived three economic eras and says plainly that Google's construction phases are why his hotel is still open. To shoot: a working spa with guests and staff, and a boat moored beside the hotel that seats ten, which is the only way to get the campus from the water. Prefers Finnish. Parking at the hotel and at his house. Filming is booked separately for Mon 17.
Prep — background and 4 priority questions
Owner, SpaHotel Hamina. 60s, born and bred. His career mirrors Finland's swings — family jewellery business bought out of a 1990s bankruptcy, first in Finland to sell jewellery online, store closed 2022. Founded the hotel 2002; Russian tourism collapsed after 2014 and again in 2022 with the border. He credits Google's construction phases with the hotel surviving. Measured critic of platform market power (Booking.com's ~17% commissions inside Google's ad ecosystem) rather than of Google itself.
Entry pointOpen on the town before the campus and let him walk it forward through his own books. Do not open on Google.
Priority questions
  • Which construction phases filled the rooms, in which years, and roughly what share of occupancyThe cleanest halo chain we have. Get years, not adjectives.
  • The permission-to-ask-again closeHe named 17 Aug himself for filming. Reconcile it at the table and log YES / OPEN / NO.
  • Who in Kotka, and who does the campus touch that we'd never think ofHe recommended Ville Meronen originally; he will have more.
  • Answer his own question: how many of us are coming to breakfastHe asked, and it affects his table booking.
Scheduling detail
CONFIRMED in writing 7 Aug: “August 12th at 9am fits me well.” Sapir's invite is now issued to him directly (not a HOLD) at 9:00–9:30 Finland, venue the hotel. He asks how many people are coming — answer owed, he says next week is fine. Alignment-call read: a strong candidate for a longer follow-around on a filming day, and only the half hour has been asked for.

For Nick & the crewThe independent environmental voice, and the reason the film survives a sceptical viewer. Measured rather than adversarial: she says on record that Google's presence is positive overall and that building on the old mill site rather than untouched land was right, and her ask is constructive. Calm, evidence-led, scientific background. VISUALS: the best observational material on the slate — beekeeping in the hives, walking the 60 hectares of forest she has protected for twenty years. Golden-hour woodland against server halls is the contrast shot of the market. Prefers Finnish, films at home in Summa. Nature is observation only in the room — never ask her to confirm a biodiversity outcome either way.
Prep — background and 3 priority questions
Regional Secretary, Finnish Association for Nature Conservation (SE Finland). Master's in Philosophy, bioindicator research background, evidence-led, avoids inflammatory language. On record that Google's presence is positive overall and that redeveloping the Summa mill site rather than untouched land was the right call. Her critique is specific — 2020 Petkelvuori quarrying and Siberian flying-squirrel habitat, a formal complaint against the City's environmental department — and her ask is constructive. Beekeeper of 30+ years, manages 60 hectares of naturally-managed forest.
Entry pointObservation, not verdict. She is measured; match it.
Priority questions
  • What she has observed on the ground, over what period, and how she recorded itObservation with a method behind it is the only environmental material we can carry.
  • The Petkelvuori complaint — what she asked for and what happenedSpecific, documented, and hers to tell.
  • Her old-growth offset proposal, in her own framingThe constructive ask is the part that survives a sceptical viewer.
HandlingAsk her to describe what she has seen. Never ask her to confirm whether wildlife is better or worse off.
Scheduling detail
THE GAP SHE FILLS — Amy Murphy flagged on 5 Aug that every environmental fact we hold for Hamina comes from Google or the City, and that Hamina is worse than Pryor on this. Kimmo went beyond the contact list and found the independent voice unprompted. She is the careful version of it: Master's in Philosophy, bioindicator research background, evidence-led, avoids inflammatory language, and says on the record that Google's presence is positive overall and that redeveloping the Summa mill site rather than untouched land was the right call. Her critique is specific — the 2020 Petkelvuori quarrying and the Siberian flying squirrel habitat, a formal complaint against the City's environmental department, and a constructive ask that Google offset habitat loss by protecting old-growth forest elsewhere in Finland. Beekeeper of 30+ years, manages 60 hectares of naturally-managed forest — strong observational filming. Prefers Finnish. HANDLING: never ask her or anyone to confirm a biodiversity outcome in either direction; nature is something we ask her to describe, never to confirm. Let Sarah and Adria know she is on the slate before the day, as a courtesy rather than a permission ask. BOOKED 10 Aug — and the venue is not where this board said it was. She and her husband keep two homes: the childhood house in Summa, and Virolahti, where the beehives and the protected forest actually are. The shoot is Virolahti, Koivuniemetie 160 A — 40 minutes out, so the crew leaves at 7:15 for an 8:00 arrival, interview 9:15–10:00, beekeeping and the forest walk 10:15–11:30, back in Hamina by 12:30. The Summa framing survives as her history, not as the location.
